clue.text: Judge newly headed this large organisation

explanation.surface: A judge has just taken charge of some big institution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newly headed' says the first letter of UMPIRE is replaced; the clue leaves the new letter, E, for the solver to find from the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An empire can be a large business group under one controlling owner, as in a media empire.

clue.text: Visual faculty certainly needed in rowing crew

indicators.note: needed in, so the word for certainly goes inside the crew

parts.note: an eight is a racing boat crewed by eight rowers
yes is an emphatic certainly

explanation.surface: Good vision is surely essential for a rowing team.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesight is the power of seeing, the sense of vision.

clue.text: Star and manger, apt somehow

explanation.surface: A Nativity scene: the star over the manger is fitting in some way.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentagram is a five-pointed star drawn with five straight lines.

clue.text: Keep terriers in check

indicators.note: the abbreviation for terriers is put inside the word for check

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
Terriers is the nickname for members of Britain's Territorial Army, abbreviated TA

explanation.surface: Hold the dogs back on a lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terriers' are soldiers of the Territorial Army (TA), Britain's volunteer reserve, not dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: To retain is to hold on to something rather than lose it.

clue.text: Item of jewellery worn by lady abroad with boldness

clue.text: Like a school governor, beyond understanding?

explanation.surface: A school board's oversight is hard to fathom.
explanation.definitionFit: A governing body ranks over a headteacher; and something too difficult to grasp is said to go over your comprehension.

clue.text: I'm finished with old painting technique

parts.note: something finished is over, in the past

explanation.surface: A retired artist says they're done with an outdated way of painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is the laying on of paint so thickly that brush marks stand out from the canvas.

clue.text: Fresh information about being imprisoned

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
re means about or concerning

explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Green can mean new or unseasoned, as fresh produce or a raw recruit is.

clue.text: Poodles son brought into country

indicators.note: put inside, so the abbreviation for son goes within the country

parts.note: Yemen is a country in the Arabian Peninsula

explanation.surface: Someone's boy imports pet dogs into a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'poodle' is a servile follower, as a politician is called another leader's poodle.
explanation.definitionFit: Toadies who always agree with their boss are obsequious lackeys, figuratively called poodles.

clue.text: An artist long ago, name being collected

indicators.note: the letter for name is gathered up inside the word for long ago

parts.note: erst is an old word meaning formerly or long ago

explanation.walkthrough: Max Ernst was a German-born Surrealist painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a leading Dada and Surrealist painter, so he is one example of an artist.

clue.text: Late news to pack in crowd

parts.note: to pack something in is to stop doing it
to press is to crowd or push against

explanation.surface: Breaking news of a stampede to cram into a crush of people.

clue.text: Nonpareil, by inference, this apple?

explanation.surface: An apple so perfect you need not look elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unequalled is so good you need look no more for better; it is also the name of an old English apple variety.

clue.text: Fancy goods originally imported by one US state

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the original letter of goods, its first

explanation.surface: Luxury merchandise first shipped in by a single American state.

clue.text: Vital element of German city church

parts.note: Essen is a city in the Ruhr region of Germany
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church in a German city is said to be a key part of life there.
explanation.definitionFit: The essence of something is its most important, indispensable quality.

clue.text: Injure husband with weapon

parts.note: an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

explanation.surface: A wife is told to hurt her spouse with a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: To harm someone is to hurt or damage them.

clue.text: From time to time, see the two sides at Old Trafford?

definitions.text: the two sides at Old Trafford?

explanation.surface: Watching a Manchester match, play seems to stop and start.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Trafford in Manchester is a cricket ground; in cricket, the field is split into the leg side (also called the on side) and the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something intermittently means now and then; and the on side and off side are the two halves of a cricket field.

clue.text: Go-between who doesn't charge? His actions are not constrained by others

explanation.definitionFit: A free agent is someone independent who can act as he pleases.

clue.text: Pictures of gold cross beneath altar

parts.note: the altar in church is also called the communion table
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
X is shaped like a cross

explanation.surface: Images of a golden cross set below a church altar.
explanation.definitionFit: Tableaux are striking scenes or groupings, like living pictures staged by motionless performers.

clue.text: Reveal list of passengers flying

explanation.surface: Show the airline roster of travellers.
explanation.definitionFit: To manifest is to show plainly; a manifest is also the document listing an aircraft's cargo or travellers.

clue.text: Carp in prison about it, privacy primarily

parts.note: nick is British slang for prison

indicators.note: first of all, the opening letter of privacy

explanation.walkthrough: 'Carp' looks like the fish but is the verb to complain. NICK is British slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to find fault over petty details, to quibble.

clue.text: Cheese knife taster is holding

clue.text: Pope's ambassador on at leader of episcopalians

indicators.note: the leading letter of episcopalians

explanation.surface: A papal envoy rides at the head of a group of Anglican churchgoers.

clue.text: Umpire arrives carrying snack

parts.note: arr is the timetable abbreviation for arrives

explanation.surface: The match official turns up holding a light meal.

clue.text: Anger about book, authoritative book

indicators.note: around, so the anger word surrounds the abbreviation for book

parts.note: bile is bitterness or anger

explanation.definitionFit: A bible is any work regarded as the standard reference on its subject.

clue.text: Confront the old bishop with everything after end of service

the final letter of the word service

all means everything

parts.note: to sneer is to speak scornfully

clue.text: Explosive male in group facing former partner
